about: The surroundings' shared vectors (brief M4-02, m4-design §2; the game's reader comes in a later brief): tests/shared/surroundings_fixture/ is a synthetic world (origin E 2618250 / N 1101750, height_offset_m 1250.25, the owner's axes, area 'fixture' E 2616000-2625000, N 1095000-1107000: 9 km x 12 km) and nine synthetic swissALTIRegio tiles at a 1000 m cell (source.json; invented heights, no swisstopo data). surroundings.json grows the area by margin_m 3000 at spacing_m 3000: the box E 2613000-2628000, N 1092000-1110000, 6 columns x 7 rows, rows north to south, columns west to east; vertex (row r, column c) is LV95 (e_min + 3000 c, n_max - 3000 r), local x = E - 2618250, z = -(N - 1101750). Its height is the largest sample whose position lies in [E - 1500, E + 1500) x [N - 1500, N + 1500), minus 1250.25, rounded once to float32; a vertex strictly inside the area box is NaN (the quiet NaN 0x7FC00000, bytes 00 00 c0 7f). The 1000 m cells put samples on the squares' edges, which the live 10 m data at 100 m never does: the half-open rule is decided here. Computed by design two independent ways (numpy; plain Python in whole centimetres), identical bytes. local_y is the float32 value written as a decimal exactly.

vertices.note: north-west corner. Its highest sample is on its square's west edge (x = E - 1500, included); the higher ones on its east edge (x = E + 1500, column 1's) and its north edge (y = N + 1500, no vertex's) are not its own
